methods.label: Substitute and show the remaining factor is positive
methods.explanation:
At an intersection, both equations hold, so use \(y=2-x\) to eliminate \(y\):
\[
\frac8{x^2+4}=2-x.
\]
For every real \(x\), the denominator \(x^2+4\) is positive. Multiplying by it is therefore valid and gives
\[
8=(2-x)(x^2+4).
\]
Expanding and rearranging, then factoring out \(x\), gives
\[
0=x^3-2x^2+4x=x(x^2-2x+4).
\]
To see whether the second factor can vanish, complete its square:
\[
x^2-2x+4=(x-1)^2+3>0.
\]
Thus the product can be zero only when \(x=0\). This gives \(y=2\), which satisfies both original equations. The unique real intersection therefore has \(x=0\), choice C.
